title: Back-Rank Mate
concept: A king hiding behind its own pawns can get locked in its own house.

glossary.definition: A player's first row: row 1 for White, row 8 for Black. Kings often get stuck there behind their own pawns.

summary: Look for a king stuck behind its own pawns, then check it on the back row. And give your own king some air: push one pawn so it has an escape square.

narration: Black's knight jumps to f4 to bother your pieces. But it was the only piece that could hop back to f8 and block a check on the back row.
Rook takes d8, checkmate! The king wants to escape, but its own pawns on f7, g7 and h7 block every door.

guided.hint: White's king is stuck behind its own pawns. Can one of your rooks reach row 1?
guided.explanation: Rook to d1, checkmate on the back row! The king's own pawns block every escape, and White's rook on a1 can't take: your bishop on b1 is in the way.

guided.hint: White's king on h1 is boxed in by its own pawns. Which of your pieces can reach row 1?
guided.explanation: Queen to d1, checkmate! The pawns on g2 and h2 lock the king in, and nothing can get in the way on e1, f1 or g1.

guided.hint: Black's rook just took on e8. Your other rook can take back. What happens to the king then?
guided.explanation: Rook takes e8, checkmate! The king can't step forward because of its own pawns, and your queen on d6 guards f8. Two pieces, one trap.
